repaired_pre_existing_gate.note: This is a repair of a gate the extraction broke, not a weakening of it. The retargeted mutant was confirmed killed, and a `cmp -s` guard now makes the same rot fail loudly instead of passing silently. Every other `sed -i` anchor in test/packet_frontend/Makefile and test/Makefile was audited and still occurs the expected number of times.
repaired_pre_existing_gate.symptom: The last sub-mutation of test/packet_frontend/Makefile's `mutation:` target anchored on `frame_opcode == OP_SET && frame_length != 51`, which the extraction moved out of lsc1_packet_frontend.sv into the validator's length table. The sed therefore edited nothing, the mutant was byte-identical to the original, and it 'survived' -- a gate that had silently stopped testing.
repaired_pre_existing_gate.repair: Retargeted at asic_core/rtl/lsc1_request_validator.sv (`OP_SET: expected_length = 16'd51;` -> `= frame_length;`) and added a `cmp -s` 'edited nothing' guard. The downstream assertion `grep -q "status got=87 expected=83"` is unchanged and still holds.
